title: The UK will help Ukraine make long-range missiles by sharing classified tech information
description: Burnham, who was in Kyiv for Ukraine's Independence Day, said defense firm MBDA will release details on U.K.-made parts for the SCALP missile to Ukraine to help the country assemble the weapons.

title: US set for largest mass visa revocation in history targeting up to 200,000 foreigners, officials say
description: The Trump administration is preparing to revoke the business and tourism visas of up to 200,000 foreigners who have applied for or are currently seeking asylum status in the United States.

title: Log Cabin Republicans remove reference to trans people on website
description: The Republican gay rights group has decided to no longer focus on transgender issues.

title: Trump moves to reshape White House’s South Lawn
description: The president's latest construction project involves changing the lawn's slope to bring it flush with his new helipad.

title: What’s happening between the U.S. and Canada
description: And what it could mean for the American economy.

title: An aluminum smelter becomes part of Oklahoma Republican governor runoff election
description: A proposed $4 billion aluminum smelter pushed by President Trump is splitting Oklahoma Republicans.

title: Supreme Court gives Trump an interim win on his mail voting order, but hurdles loom
description: The Supreme Court paused a lower court's ruling that blocked key parts of Trump's order to limit voting by mail for the midterms. But U.S. Postal Service work on the order remains blocked nationwide.

title: See photos from the first IndyCar race in Washington
description: Drivers are dashing around the National Mall at speeds expected to exceed 185 mph.

title: This not-so-secret document is inspiring the left — and tripping up its candidates
description: The Democratic Socialists of America platform aims to upend the status quo. That can mean a bumpy ride for those trying to win in the short term.

title: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveils new U.S. economic sanctions to isolate Iran
description: The Trump administration calls this an "economic D-Day" on Iran. Iran vows to respond to fresh sanctions in a "seismic manner."

title: How Trump's foreign policy is affecting America's relationship with its allies
description: NPR's Leila Fadel asks New York Times White House correspondent Peter Baker for his analysis of President Trump's foreign policy.

title: Secret White House bunker undercuts Trump’s ballroom lawsuit, ex-officials say
description: The White House already has a nuclear-proof facility buried deep underground and built in secret after 9/11.

title: Trump’s visa ban on 75 countries struck down by federal judge
description: A federal judge said the indefinite pause, which affected nationals of countries in every corner of the globe, ran afoul of antidiscrimination protections.

title: Pence says U.S.-Canada trade fight adds to affordability concerns for economy
description: “I think the last thing we need right now, as our economy is getting back on its feet, is a trade war with Canada,” the former vice president told CNN.

title: El-Sayed’s win triggered wave of anti-Muslim rhetoric online, Post analysis shows
description: After Abdul El-Sayed won the Democratic Senate nomination in Michigan, conservative commentary about him shifted focus from socialism to his Muslim identity.

title: Becerra, running for governor of California, faces a health insurance problem
description: The nation's uninsured rate hit a historical low when Xavier Becerra was health secretary. Now he wants to be California's next governor as Trump's actions have driven people off health insurance.

title: Trump nominates Cameron Hamilton to lead FEMA (again)
description: NPR's Ayesha Rascoe asks "Politico's" Thomas Frank about new FEMA administrator Cameron Hamilton and whether his appointment means a change in heart by the Trump administration about the agency.

title: Week in politics: primaries results, Iran pressure, Korean relations flip
description: Democrats have not shown a clear preference for progressive candidates over moderate ones. Republicans have rejected some of President Trump's endorsees despite his tight grip on the party's base.

title: The complexities of covering swing voters and what they teach us about politics
description: For Reporter's Notebook, an NPR political correspondent shares the lessons she has learned listening in on groups of swing voters in swing states.
